sourceReviews.notes: The Windows WinExe has the per-launch normal/modded chooser, installation discovery and validation, explicit --game-mode/--game-path parsing, dashboard lifetime and graceful game-loss shutdown in App.xaml.cs, GameRuntimeMode.cs and MainWindow.xaml.cs. RuntimeModeTests and the Host GameStartupCliTailParityTests cover chooser policy, parser forms, discovery, compatibility, auto-navigation gating, automation command parsing and retired Host options. The App parser itself accepts only mode/path and silently ignores Mac App auto-navigation, automation-control, retired and command-mode arguments; corresponding utilities live partly in the separate Host. Windows also has no Mac-equivalent newest-instance retirement. Full launched-WinExe lifecycle remains unverified.

MainWindow.xaml and MainWindow.xaml.cs provide Auto Save plus named-state listing, size/age metadata, Save State, New, Delete, Load and Hacker atlas deletion. AtlasStateStore, VisionResetController, AtlasStateStoreParityTests, ActiveAtlasReplacementTests and the autosave-age regression cover immutable states, permanent storage removal, archival, active-world replacement, rollback and reset invalidation. The active Auto Save reset confirms and keeps a recoverable backup, but named-state Delete and Hacker Delete Atlas execute without the destructive confirmation required by the Mac view. The complete rendered manager workflow has no direct UI regression.

GdiWindowCapture captures the Windows client rectangle as cursor-free BGRA, and CpuBgraNormalizer produces the canonical 640x360 frame. ObjectDetectionIntegrationTests exercises real non-client chrome, genuinely tall clients and cursor exclusion; core tests cover exact, wide and tall crops. Windows MainWindow targets a 33 ms loop (about 30 Hz), not Mac native/60 Hz capture, and has no equivalent explicit four-frame object-inference sampling contract. Queueing and live cadence therefore remain platform-divergent despite equivalent crop/cursor behavior.

The platform-equivalent path is GdiWindowCapture plus FrameGeometry and CpuBgraNormalizer: client-only top-origin BGRA is center-cropped to 16:9, resampled to 640x360 and retains capture identity. Program tests cover exact/wide/tall crop, projection center and channel-preserving solid normalization; ObjectDetectionIntegrationTests verifies title-bar exclusion against real Windows windows. Windows uses raw per-channel BGRA bilinear interpolation, whereas Mac preserves Core Image color management and can fail createCGImage conversion; no pixel differential or failure-path coverage establishes equivalence. Windows tracking consumes the canonical frame directly, so a separate solveWidth result is unnecessary.

HollowKnightWindowLocator.cs ports GameWindowCandidate and GameWindowSelection with the same exact normalized-title preference followed by largest nonnegative client area among non-minimized candidates. UI Program tests map both Mac cases: gameplay beats a Unity helper, and untitled candidates fall back to largest area. Production locator uses that selection result and adds a Windows-specific minimized-last adaptation before applying the shared ordering.

GroundCameraSolver.cs and GroundCameraSolver.Matching.cs port the acceptance, innovation, promotion, cadence, provisional/trusted reference, owned evidence, spatial handoff, patch matching, correction and rollback behavior. All 25 direct Mac GroundCameraSolver tests map to GroundCameraSolverTests; BroadRecentConsensusParityTests, GroundLongRowParityTests and GroundTrackingEdgeParityTests add production-edge coverage. VisualGameplayTracker constructs the calibrated keyframe-subpixel solver used by Mac production tracking.

Mac LiveCaptureModel launches GroundFrameAudit and records it whenever hypothesis tracking exists. Windows has no GroundFrameAudit or --ground-audit-directory producer, so the reachable bounded asynchronous PNG-plus-JSON evidence stream and its tracking serialization are absent. GroundSceneAuditParityTests can consume optional stored evidence but do not produce it.

GroundLineDetector.cs ports edge analysis, paired comparison, theory stages, semantic lines, foreground rejection, debug/stage images and presence filtering. GroundDetectionEfficiencyTests, GroundReferenceDetectorParityTests, GroundEarlyRecognitionTests, GroundSurfaceEvidenceTests, GroundLinePresenceTests and mapped Program regressions cover the production detector algorithms extensively. Mac live UI also presents Edge, Detect and presence-based Cleaned diagnostic images; Windows MainWindow exposes only Ground Features, never presents its Edge/Detect/Cleaned helpers, and has no PresenceImage equivalent. Detector behavior is mapped, but those reachable diagnostics are missing.

GroundPoseRefinementSearch.cs has the same radius, evidence thresholds, error/inlier/distance ordering and spatially distinct near-rival rejection. GroundPoseRefinementSearchTests maps all three Mac cases: sub-cell XY recovery, repeated-texture ambiguity and small occluded consensus rejection. Production GroundHypothesisTracker calls the implementation.

GroundSubpixelRegistration.cs ports the disjoint fit/validation samples, contrast normalization, robust loss, bounded damped refinement and independent validation gates; GroundCameraSolver.Matching integrates it. GroundSubpixelTests maps all three Mac cases for fractional recovery, integrated publication, exact integer motion and flat-frame rejection.

BgraPngReader.cs and PngWriter.cs provide the reviewed Windows BGRA-to-PNG and PNG-to-BGRA paths. Program.TestPngWriter and SceneSessionStoreTests.TestPNGSourcePreservesBlackAndAlphaPixels verify PNG writing and black/alpha round trips. Unlike ImageIO, the Windows decoder accepts only non-interlaced 8-bit RGBA PNG rather than the broader image formats supported by CGImageSource; cross-platform codec coverage therefore remains partial.

LabelingExampleStore.cs owns the same shared identifiers and exact 17-entry legacy alias table, canonical pass-through and equality semantics. LabelingEditorPolicyParityTests covers legacy ownership, while ExampleStoreTests.TestLegacySelectMigration, TestLegacyGameSplit and TestCanonicalSnapshotPersistence cover migration and stored canonical identity. Windows intentionally rejects blank identifiers at storage boundaries without changing valid identity behavior.

LiveTrackingTimingPolicies.cs ports pose prediction, measured-ground evidence, capture-ground reliability, transition publication, floorless handoff and floorless candidate selection; all 11 LiveTrackingTimingParityTests map those policies. FramePipelineTelemetry and its tests cover bounded stage statistics. Some policy coverage is offline-only, and Windows lacks Mac LivePresentationTiming image-identity provenance plus capture-to-publish, capture-to-draw, GPU queue/execution and draw-to-present instrumentation in the live renderer.

MainWindow.xaml OpsPanel, MainWindow query/apply handlers, MainWindow.LabelPause.cs and WindowsGameControlForwarder.PerformPlayerOpsAsync port the bounded PlayerOps controls, receiver protocol, apply/query flow and label-pause restoration. InputBridgeParityTests and Program.TestReceiverPlayerOps cover core state normalization and wire round trips. Windows UI randomization chooses Geo uniformly from 0 through 9999 instead of the Mac equal digit-length bands, and the core randomization test does not exercise that UI handler. Windows requires explicit Apply while Mac steppers apply immediately; its toggle also defaults false, is not persisted, an older concurrent acknowledgement can overwrite newer UI state, and the view has no equivalent busy disabling or red error presentation.

Windows has no RawGroundFrameAudit or --ground-raw-audit-directory implementation. GroundSceneAuditParityTests consumes optional evidence but does not produce raw luma/JSON pairs. The one-pending-write bound, skipped-frame count, 6000-frame cap, periodic feature-bank snapshots, cleanup and CLI activation are absent.

OnnxObjectDetector.NormalizedBox.IntersectionOverUnion, LabelingReviewAnalysis and LiveObjectDetection use the same intersection-over-union formula and zero-area handling. ReviewAnalysisTests exercises overlap matching and LiveObjectDetection tests exercise the operation through classwise NMS. Equivalence is established for standardized or otherwise validated production inputs; this does not claim identical behavior for arbitrary invalid rectangles.

GameRuntimeModeValue.cs, GameRuntimeMode.cs, HollowKnightGameLauncher.cs and App.xaml.cs port mode values, per-launch choice, installation compatibility/discovery and normal/modded selection. Seven RuntimeModeTests plus Program.TestRuntimeModeLaunchPolicy and TestGameInstallationDiscovery cover the principal contracts. Windows GameLaunchOptions rejects repeated --game-mode but repeated --game-path silently uses the last value, whereas Mac throws a repeated-path error; launched chooser and platform discovery still lack full end-to-end verification.

MainWindow.xaml supplies shared native WPF segmented RadioButton styling, and the UI TestModeSelection regression verifies radio groups, common styling, programmatic selection and selected styling through hover. The Mac wrapper's equal-width segment distribution, fixed 24-point fitting, accessibility label and stability under continuous live-frame updates have no equivalent rendered or automation verification on Windows.

UserObjectCatalog.cs and MainWindow catalog/add/model integration port schema-1 persistence, slug identifiers, aliases, atomic saving and shared-model inclusion; Program.TestUserObjectCatalog covers the principal happy path. Custom choices are exposed only in Game, with the Mac Enemies/World context filtering absent.

VisionResetController.cs and MainWindow reset handlers archive reset targets, invalidate and drain active workers, and preserve gameplay data during stencil reset. Context inference, fresh introduced-class snapshots on save/update, canonical aliases/options split, sorted unique migration persistence, training class/context queries independent of Draft/Ready, known-empty evidence, normalized reverse-drag boxes, language/capture metadata preservation, atomic save/update and selected-directory deletion have direct regressions. All 13 Mac recorder regressions are ported and mapped: thread-safe lifecycle, deduplicated overlapping input, held-key closure, backward-compatible diagnostics, 20 Hz low-resolution trace cap, exact-capture ground reliability and atlas admission, unverified samples, safe atomic named storage, button conversion, replay validation including hero-less cutscenes, and bounded command parsing.
